text:
Choose the correct set of reagents for the following conversion.

trans $(\mathrm{Ph}-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_{3})\to \mathrm{cis}(\mathrm{Ph}-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_{3})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Converting the trans alkene into the cis alkene requires going through the alkyne, which is then reduced by syn addition of $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}$.

$\mathrm{Br}{}_{2}$ adds across the C=C bond to give $\mathrm{Ph}-\mathrm{CHBr}-\mathrm{CHBr}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ (1,2-dibromo-1-phenylpropane).

Alcoholic KOH eliminates one HBr to give a vinyl bromide, and $\mathrm{NaNH}{}_{2}$ eliminates the second HBr to give the alkyne $\mathrm{Ph}-\mathrm{C}\equiv \mathrm{C}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$. Aqueous KOH favours substitution of Br by OH rather than elimination, so options (B) and (D) fail at this step.

$\mathrm{H}{}_{2}$ over Lindlar catalyst ($\mathrm{Pd}/\mathrm{CaCO}{}_{3}$ poisoned with quinoline) delivers both H atoms to the same face of the triple bond, giving cis-$\mathrm{Ph}-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$. Na in liquid $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ would give the trans alkene again, so option (C) fails.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift

text:
Cobalt chloride when dissolved in water forms pink colored complex $\mathrm{X}–$ which has
octahedral geometry. This solution on treating with conc $\mathrm{HCl}$ forms deep blue complex, $\mathrm{Y}–$ which has a $\mathrm{Z}–$ geometry. $\mathrm{X},\mathrm{Y}$ and $\mathrm{Z}$, respectively, are
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In water, $\mathrm{CoCl}{}_{2}$ gives the pink octahedral aqua complex $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{6}]{}^{2+}$, with cobalt in the +2 state ($3d^{7}$).

Concentrated HCl supplies a large excess of $\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$, which replaces the water ligands without changing the oxidation state; four of the large $\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$ ions surround $\mathrm{Co}{}^{2+}$ tetrahedrally, giving the deep blue complex.

$[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{6}]{}^{2+}+4\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}[\mathrm{CoCl}{}_{4}]{}^{2-}+6\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

The options with $[\mathrm{CoCl}{}_{6}]{}^{3-}$, $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{6}]{}^{3+}$ or $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{4}\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}]{}^{+}$ need Co(III), which is not formed because neither water nor HCl oxidises Co(II).

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift

text:
The logarithm of equilibrium constant for the reaction $\mathrm{Pd}^{2+}+4\mathrm{Cl}^{-}⇌\mathrm{PdCl}_{4}^{2-}$ is $___________ ($Nearest integer)

Given : $\frac{2.303R\mathrm{T}}{\mathrm{F}}=0.06\mathrm{V}$

$\mathrm{Pd}_{(\mathrm{aq})}^{2+}+2\mathrm{e}^{-}⇌\mathrm{Pd}(\mathrm{s})\mathrm{E}^{⊖}=0.83\mathrm{V}$

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{PdCl}_{4}^{2-}(\mathrm{aq})+2\mathrm{e}^{-}⇌\mathrm{Pd}(\mathrm{s})+4\mathrm{Cl}^{-}(\mathrm{aq})\mathrm{E}^{⊖}=0.65\mathrm{V} \end{array}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The required reaction is the sum of a reduction and an oxidation:

$\mathrm{Pd}{}^{2+}+2\mathrm{e}{}^{-}\longrightarrow \mathrm{Pd}(\mathrm{s})E_{\text{red}}^{\circ }=0.83\text{V (cathode)}$

$\mathrm{Pd}(\mathrm{s})+4\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}\longrightarrow \mathrm{PdCl}{}_{4}{}^{2-}+2\mathrm{e}{}^{-}E_{\text{red}}^{\circ }(\mathrm{PdCl}{}_{4}{}^{2-}/\mathrm{Pd})=0.65\text{V (anode)}$

Adding them gives $\mathrm{Pd}{}^{2+}+4\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}\mathrm{PdCl}{}_{4}{}^{2-}$ with $n=2$ and

$E_{\text{cell}}^{\circ }=E_{\text{cathode}}^{\circ }-E_{\text{anode}}^{\circ }=0.83-0.65=0.18\text{V}$

From $\Delta G^{\circ }=-nFE_{\text{cell}}^{\circ }=-2.303RT\log K$:

$\log K=\dfrac{nE_{\text{cell}}^{\circ }}{0.06}=\dfrac{2\times 0.18}{0.06}=6$

Hence, the answer is 6.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift
